measurement1_whatIsExposedAndWhere.rule: A privacy claim about an artifact nobody retains is a different problem from one about a sealed durable record. Every row below names the persisted schema, the JSON path in the live vector, and the retention character as far as it could be established.

durableRows.scale: O(|S|) -- one entry per subject in the no-match or aggregate-match scope
durableRows.retentionCharacter: PERSISTED by declaration (it is in persistedSchemaRegistry) and REQUIRED (not optional). It must be retained because EP-4 recomputes the commitment from it.

durableRows.notPartOfDIV2: DIV-2 as filed is about the subject-SET commitment. X-2 is a separate durable path-text position that the DIV-2 framing does not name. It is recorded because a posture decision that fixes X-1 and not X-2 would be a partial fix, and because the two have different justifications: a match proof must say WHERE the match is -- that is the witness and it is the point of the claim -- whereas a no-match proof carries the entire subject inventory to prove a negative. The privacy weight is not equal.
durableRows.additionalDisclosure: The value carries a symbol suffix after '#'. threat-model.v3#findings[3] (V4) is verbatim: 'Symbol and identifier names can themselves be PII -- a function named for a real customer, a fixture constant holding an email.'

durableRows.scale: O(1) per local match, OPTIONAL on LocalMatchProofV2
durableRows.whatItAdds: position within the named file. Combined with X-2 it locates a construct, not merely a file.

durableRows.note: In the live vector these are namespaced identifiers, not paths. See measurement1.theVocabularyIsNotUNIFORM.

transientRows.what: the SubjectV1 leaf record and its leaf hash
transientRows.grammar: evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.records[SubjectV1]: recordTag 0x13, one field 'value' at tag 0x05, encoding componentFrame(text), presence required. Golden: preimageGoldens.records[EP5-REC-SUBJECT].encodedHex = 1305000000087372632f612e7473, whose trailing 8 bytes are the literal ASCII 'src/a.ts'.
transientRows.retentionCharacter: TRANSIENT. SubjectV1 does not appear in persistedSchemaRegistry. It is constructed during commitment computation from the retained members and discarded. Only the 32-byte root, inside the outer frame, survives as the commitment string.
transientRows.consequence: The original DIV-2 framing -- 'raw path text in the leaf' -- names a transient object. The durable exposure is X-1. This is the whole of the second correction and it is verified.

theVocabularyIsNotUNIFORM_measured.finding: evaluation-proof.v8 does not SPECIFY that a subject is a path. It specifies unconstrained text, and exhibits BOTH path-like and namespaced-identifier subjects in its own positive vectors.
theVocabularyIsNotUNIFORM_measured.measured: All 11 subject-bearing values across the 7 positive vectors were extracted and classified against fact-plane.v1#factRecordContractV1.relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1.sharedTypes.SubjectIdV1, verbatim: 'CanonicalText containing a non-empty lowercase ASCII namespace followed by ":" and a non-empty opaque NFC identity'. Result: 6 CONFORMANT ('pkg:a','pkg:b','sym:0','sym:1','sym:2','sym:3') and 5 NON-CONFORMANT and path-like ('src/a.ts','src/b.ts','src/c.ts','src/a.ts#f' x2). EP8-POS-AGGREGATE-WAIVED-PASS commits a partition whose members are 'sym:0'..'sym:3'; EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS commits a partition whose members are paths. Same schema, same field, two vocabularies.
theVocabularyIsNotUNIFORM_measured.thereIsNoWireGRAMMARForIt: evaluation-proof.v8#wireGrammars declares patterns for evaluationId, predicateId, projectId, contentRef, planId, activationId and closed enums for outcome, claimShape, verdict, dependencyRole -- 10 entries. It declares NOTHING for subjectId or for partition members. In the executing checker, artifacts/check-evaluation-proof.py validates each member with _string(member, path, out) called WITHOUT a pattern argument, so the admitted domain is any non-empty NFC string of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes with no C0/C1 controls. Measured directly against the live function: it admits 'src/a.ts' and it admits 'sha256:<64 hex>' equally, today, with no change to any byte.
theVocabularyIsNotUNIFORM_measured.whyThisMatters: It weakens the premise that the two postures are a specification conflict. On the bytes, evidence.v1 SPECIFIES a subject identity (a fact-tuple digest) and evaluation-proof.v8 specifies NO subject identity at all -- it specifies a frame around whatever text it is handed, and its fixtures happen to contain paths in 5 of 11 positions. The divergence is real and material, but it is a divergence between a specification and an UNDERSPECIFICATION, not between two rival specifications.
theVocabularyIsNotUNIFORM_measured.andItIsALSOAnInternalMismatch: fact-plane.v1 is a section 3 binding-table member (freeze section 3 row 'FACT-PLANE / C-1', PASSED with changes, SEAL candidate). Its SubjectIdV1 requires a 'namespace:' prefix. evaluation-proof.v8's own EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS members do not satisfy it. Either the two artifacts mean different things by 'subject', or one of them is wrong. This brief could not determine which -- see whatCouldNotBeDetermined.U-4.

measurement2_whatAHolderOfTheArtifactLea.rule: Stated as what is inferable, not as what is alarming. Every figure is measured on this repository on 2026-08-04 or read from a live vector.

directly: the complete relative-path inventory of every subject in scope -- file names and directory names, verbatim
the project's directory structure and depth
file extensions, and therefore languages, frameworks and build systems in use

Absolute paths and usernames, IF the subject value is a fact-plane CanonicalPath -- fact-plane.v1#...sharedTypes.CanonicalPath is verbatim 'non-empty NFC project-relative path, slash separators, no empty/dot/dot-dot segment, no leading slash or backslash'. A project-relative path cannot carry a home directory or a username.

IMPORTANT QUALIFIER: that protection comes from FACT-PLANE, not from evaluation-proof.v8. evaluation-proof.v8 imposes NO grammar on members (measured: zero wireGrammars entries for subject values), so nothing in evaluation-proof.v8 itself prevents an absolute path, a home directory or a username from being committed and retained. The instruction's question 'possibly usernames or absolute paths' resolves to: NOT under FACT-PLANE's path type; NOT PREVENTED by evaluation-proof.v8's own grammar. Which of the two governs a production subject could not be determined -- see whatCouldNotBeDetermined.U-4.

underTheDIGESTposture_measuredNotAssumed.theClaimBeingTested: that replacing path text with a digest makes the retained artifact non-disclosing.
underTheDIGESTposture_measuredNotAssumed.MEASURED_itDoesNOTHoldAgainstADictionary: A digest-leaf bundle still lists one entry per subject. An adversary holding that bundle and any candidate path list confirms membership by hashing each candidate and looking it up. Executed on this repository: 515 subjects, a candidate list of the 515 true paths, 515 of 515 confirmed, elapsed under 1 millisecond. File paths are a low-entropy, highly guessable preimage domain -- 'src/index.ts', 'package.json', 'README.md' and their neighbours are guessable without any knowledge of the project.
underTheDIGESTposture_measuredNotAssumed.theCorpusAlreadySaysThis: threat-model.v3#findings[3].detail is verbatim: 'Content-addressing does not anonymise anything; it just makes the copy durable and deduplicated.' The measurement above is that sentence, executed.
underTheDIGESTposture_measuredNotAssumed.MEASURED_itDoesNOTShrinkTheArtifact: For this repository's 515 files: raw path text 28,012 bytes, as a JSON string array 30,072 bytes; the same list as 'sha256:'+64hex text forms is 36,565 bytes. The digest form is LARGER by about 22%, because a canonical digest text form is 71 bytes while the mean path here is 54.4 bytes. On the 3-member live vector the same holds: SubjectV1 records are 14 bytes each as paths and 77 bytes each as digest text.
whatItDOESChange: an artifact holder who does NOT already have a candidate path list learns |S| and nothing else legible -- casual reading, accidental inclusion in a support bundle, or a screenshot no longer discloses names
the artifact stops being self-describing, so disclosure now requires an adversary to bring the candidate list
it removes the symbol-name half of X-2 if applied there, which threat-model.v3#findings[3] calls out as the PII-bearing half
underTheDIGESTposture_measuredNotAssumed.theHONESTSUMMARY: digest leaves convert a plaintext disclosure into a confirmation oracle. Against an adversary who has or can guess the paths, that is close to no protection. Against inadvertent disclosure it is real protection. Both statements are true and a decision should be made against whichever adversary the threat model prioritises -- which this brief does not choose.
underTheDIGESTposture_measuredNotAssumed.andTheEVIDENCEV1LeafIsNOTAPathDigest: evidence.v1's leaf is 'the content digest of that subject's normalised fact tuple', not sha256(path). If a fact tuple embeds content-derived material its entropy is higher than a bare path and the dictionary attack costs more. The measurement above used sha256(path) because the normalised fact tuple has no definition anywhere in this corpus -- see whatCouldNotBeDetermined.U-3. That is a real limit on this measurement and it is stated rather than papered over: the dictionary result is an upper bound on the attack's ease under evidence.v1, not a measurement of it.

measurement3_doesTheMerkleFramingNeedThe.shortAnswer: NO. Measured against the executing code, not argued.

theSecondHalfOfTheGAP_confirmed.what: The sibling review's second observation was that under the promote-unchanged odd-node rule an audit path is non-uniform and its verification requires the leaf count N, which the commitment does not bind.
theSecondHalfOfTheGAP_confirmed.verified: evidence-identity-recipes.v1#R-0-typedComponentMerkleSet.steps[5] is verbatim: 'ODD NODE: if a level has an odd count, the FINAL node is PROMOTED UNCHANGED to the next level. It is NOT duplicated and NOT paired with itself.' And its observations record that evaluation-proof.v8's no-match proof carries subjectCount as a SEPARATE field the Merkle root does not bind. theSecondHalfOfTheGAP_confirmed.consequenceForADECIDER: Whoever closes DIV-2 inherits this: if non-membership proofs are wanted, an audit-path format AND a leaf-count binding must be specified, and neither exists. If they are not wanted, evidence.v1's stated rationale for sorting should be replaced by the set-canonicality rationale rather than left standing as a claim the construction cannot deliver. This brief takes no position on which.

wouldAnythingBreakIfItHeldDIGESTS.answer: NO code would break. Measured, not predicted: the live _string() gate admits a digest text form at that position today, and the live commit()/encode_subject() pair produces a well-formed commitment over digest members with no modification. The only thing that changes is the commitment VALUE, and therefore the pinned goldens.
wouldAnythingBreakIfItHeldDIGESTS.whatWouldNeedRepinning: The value sha256:65e3d109be185540e70c61c72cf072243f12cf9a37883b6797a9014255dab1c7 was searched for across the entire tree. whyThisIsARCHITECTURALLYDECISIVEForTheBr: It carries RAW PATH TEXT in the subject record -- so the plaintext posture is not confined to an unapplied candidate; a binding artifact does it too, and does it deliberately.

It is NOT a Merkle tree. It is a flat SHA-256 over deterministic-CBOR of a sorted array, under a different domain string. So the corpus already contains three distinct subject-commitment constructions, not two.

It obtains NON-MEMBERSHIP without any audit path, by holding or reconstructing the whole set. This independently corroborates measurement3: adjacent-leaf audit paths are not the only route to a universal negative, and the corpus's own binding artifact takes the other route.

MOST IMPORTANTLY: it does NOT duplicate the member rows into the proof. 'without repeating file rows in Analyze' and 'reconstruct ... from the accepted sealed manifest' are the exact shape of option OPT-3 below. The corpus already contains a worked precedent for committing to a subject set without carrying an O(|S|) copy of it alongside the commitment.
theCAVEATSThatStopThisFromBeingTheSETTLE: SCOPE. It lives entirely under typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.wireSchema -- a host-to-worker TRANSPORT contract. A wire schema is not a durable evidence artifact, and this brief did not establish that SubjectScopeV1 is ever persisted.

optionsCommonGround.theSingleMostIMPORTANTCostFinding: NO option below requires editing ANY checker's code. authorsAssessment.LABEL: THIS IS AN ASSESSMENT, NOT A DECISION, NOT A RECOMMENDATION TO ADOPT, AND NOT A SELECTION. The instruction permits stating which option the author finds strongest and requires it be clearly labelled. It is labelled. It binds nothing, and section 4.4 records what happens when a passage like this one is read as more than it is.
authorsAssessment.assessment1_theAxisIsWrong: The strongest thing this brief measured is that 'digest leaves versus plaintext leaves' is not the axis that carries the privacy weight. Three measurements say so: the leaf is TRANSIENT and appears in no persisted schema; the encoding machinery is CONTENT-AGNOSTIC and needs no code change either way; and switching to digests changes neither the artifact's size class (it grows about 22% on this repository) nor its resistance to a dictionary (515 of 515 confirmed instantly). What carries the weight is whether an O(|S|) copy of the subject inventory sits in the durable proof at all.
authorsAssessment.assessment2_whichOptionIsSTRONGEST: On the measurements, OPT-3 is the strongest -- it is the only option that restores the cost argument evidence.v1 actually made, it is the only one whose shape already has a worked precedent in a BINDING artifact (delivery.v2's reconstruct-from-sealed-manifest rule), and it is agnostic to the leaf-content question that DIV-2 is filed about. Its weakness is equally clear and is not a detail: it cannot be decided before CD-RT-5 unblocks.
authorsAssessment.assessment3_andThereforeWhat: Those two findings together do not point at a decision now. OPT-1 cannot be specified (no fact-tuple definition exists), OPT-3 cannot be decided (CD-RT-5 blocked), and OPT-2 is the status quo which needs no action to persist. The honest reading is that DIV-2 is currently BLOCKED ON INPUTS rather than blocked on judgement, and that the useful next act is to obtain the two missing inputs rather than to choose among three options two of which are gated.
authorsAssessment.assessment4_theOneThingActionableNOW: The write-time privacy class -- threat-model.v3#findings[0].requiredMitigations[1] -- is a stated obligation the current bytes measurably do not meet, and it is INDEPENDENT of which posture wins. It is the only part of this problem this brief found that is neither gated on CD-RT-5 nor gated on a missing fact-tuple definition. Stated as an observation for whoever writes the closing artifact; this brief does not propose it, schedule it, or authorise it.
whatWouldChangeThisAssessment: A definition of the normalised fact tuple. It would make OPT-1 specifiable and would let the dictionary measurement be redone against the real preimage rather than against sha256(path), which is an upper bound on the attack's ease and not a measurement of it.

Evidence that the bundle is exported off-box. That would raise the weight of all three substantive options sharply and would move the question out of retention and into egress, where the threat model has more to say.

Evidence that SubjectScopeV1 and subjectSetCommitment are one object. It would make delivery.v2 far more than a precedent -- it would make a binding artifact already carry the answer, which is the outcome the instruction warned to look for and which this brief could not establish.

whatCouldNotBeDetermined.rule: Stated plainly rather than filled in. An honest gap is worth more than a confident guess.
